I use it for everything—notes, to-dos, content planning, even managing my team. It’s super flexible, but still simple enough to not get in the way. What I love: • Pages inside pages inside pages (so clean). • Databases that actually make sense (to a non-technical person). • Easy to share with others and keep everyone on the same page. Downsides? Mobile’s still a bit clunky, and offline mode could be better. But honestly, it’s hard to beat for an all-in-one tool.

One of the most thoughtfully designed productivity tools I've used.

I use Notion to organize ideas, write documentation, and keep track of side projects. What stands out isn't just the feature set, but how well the product balances flexibility with a polished user experience.

It's a great example of how good product design can make complex workflows feel simple.

#### What needs improvement

Notion's flexibility is also one of its biggest challenges. Building a workspace from scratch can feel overwhelming, especially for new users, and it takes time to develop a system that fits your workflow.
